Implement GitHub issue #139: amount-aware import rules plus richer rule actions (set category and description). This supersedes #137, which is folded in. The full spec is below; treat it as the source of truth, but see "Spec deviations" at the end.

## Background: how import rules work today

An import rule classifies a bank-statement row (and a receipt) by matching its description against a normalized substring pattern.

- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/merchants/ImportRuleAction.scala`
  A 3-variant enum ADT: `SetMerchant(merchantId: UUID)`, `SetCategory(categoryId: UUID)`, `Ignore`. It carries exactly the data each action needs so illegal states are unrepresentable. It has a JSON `Format` (tagged object `{ "kind": ..., ... }`), a Tapir `Schema`, and `fromColumns(action, merchantId, categoryId)` which rebuilds the action from stored columns and throws loudly on a corrupt row (e.g. set_merchant with no merchant_id). There is a sibling `ImportRuleActionKind` enum.
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcher.scala`
  `Rule(id, action, pattern)`; `normalize` = lowercase + strip non-alphanumeric; `MinPatternLength = 3`; `matches` = substring; `findMatches`; `findWinner` = longest normalized pattern then most-recent UUIDv7 id. `findRowWinner(rules, description)` applies action-tier precedence ignore > set_merchant > set_category. `findReceiptWinner(rules, merchantName)` applies only set_merchant rules. `effectiveRules(explicit, merchants)` adds one virtual SetMerchant rule per merchant (merchant name as pattern), skipping merchants already covered by an explicit set_merchant rule.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/models/ImportRule.scala`
  DB model: `id, userId, action, pattern, merchantName, categoryName, autoCreated, createdAt, updatedAt`, plus `ImportRule.Create`.
- API models: `lib/api/shared/.../merchants/{CreateImportRule,UpdateImportRule,GetImportRules}.scala`.
- DAO / repo: `server/.../repositories/daos/ImportRuleDAO.scala`, `server/.../repositories/ImportRuleRepository.scala`; row DAO `BankStatementRowDAO.scala`.
- Actions: `server/.../actions/importrules/{Create,Update,Delete,GetImportRules}ImportRuleAction.scala`.
- Where matching is consumed: `server/.../services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala`, `JevStatementSuggestionsService.scala`, `TelegramExpenseService.scala`, `server/.../actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala`, `server/.../actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala`, and `lib/api/shared/.../api/utils/RowRuleVerdict.scala`.
- Frontend: `web/.../components/pages/importrules/ImportRulesPage.scala` (rule list/editor) and the bank-statement review drawer `web/.../components/pages/bankstatementreview/*` (notably `BankRowRuleForm.scala`, the create-rule-from-row path).
- A bank-statement row has a signed `amount: BigDecimal` (charge negative, credit positive), `date: LocalDate`, `description`, `txnType`.

## What to build

### 1. Amount as a match criterion (on the Rule, not the action)

Add an optional exact `amount: Option[BigDecimal]` to the rule. It is a MATCH input, shared by all action kinds, so it lives on the rule model / DB column / API models / `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule`, NOT inside an action variant.

- A rule with an amount matches only when BOTH the normalized pattern matches AND the row amount equals the rule amount exactly (no tolerance).
- Amounts are signed, so the sign is inherent in an exact match. Do not add a separate sign field.
- A rule without an amount behaves exactly as today.
- Scope is global (not account-bound). Do not add account plumbing.
- `findRowWinner` must also receive the row's amount so amount-bearing rules can be evaluated.

### 2. Richer actions (keep the 3-variant ADT)

Do NOT collapse the ADT and do NOT add a DB CHECK constraint. Enrich the variants:

- `SetMerchant(merchantId: UUID, category: Option[UUID], description: Option[String])`
- `SetCategory(categoryId: UUID, description: Option[String])`
- `Ignore`

So a set-merchant rule can optionally also set a category and/or a description; a set-category rule can optionally set a description. Update the JSON `Format`, the `Schema`, `fromColumns`, `kind`, and the helper accessors accordingly, and the DB columns + DAO + API models + Create/Update actions + ImportRulesPage editor.

Merchant default category is NOT stored on the rule and NOT resolved in the matcher or server. When `SetMerchant.category` is `None`, the FRONTEND, at the point it detects/creates the expense from the matched row, picks up the merchant's current/latest category. An explicit `category` on the rule overrides that. (Find where the frontend currently turns a set-merchant verdict into an expense's category and apply this there.)

### 3. Precedence (layered)

In `findRowWinner`: action tier first (ignore > set_merchant > set_category, unchanged), then within a tier: criteria count (a pattern+amount rule beats a pattern-only rule), then longest normalized pattern, then most-recent UUIDv7 id. Keep `findWinner`'s existing longest-then-recency behavior and layer the criteria-count ahead of it.

### 4. Receipts

A receipt sometimes carries an amount, so amount rules should apply on the receipt path too. `findReceiptWinner` takes the receipt's optional amount and evaluates amount-bearing rules the same way; when the receipt has no amount, amount-bearing rules simply do not match. The new `category` / `description` set-effects also apply on the receipt path.

### 5. Validation + UI + migration

- App-level validation only (no DB CHECK): when `amount` is present it is a valid non-zero decimal; `pattern` keeps `MinPatternLength`; the set `description` gets a sensible max length (define a limit and apply it in the API, matching how other field limits are defined in this codebase).
- UI: the rule editor and rule list/view (`ImportRulesPage`) gain amount, category, and description fields. "Create rule from this row" in the bank-statement review drawer prefills the amount (and a sensible default description). Every new view/field must be reachable from the running UI.
- Migration-safe: existing rules get null amount / category / description and behave exactly as today. Follow the project's Play Evolutions conventions.

## Project conventions (must follow)

- All DB queries (reads AND writes) include `WHERE user_id = ?`; all list queries have `ORDER BY`.
- App-level validation only; no DB CHECK constraints and no column DEFAULTs for business rules.
- Use Chimney `transformInto` for case-class shape mapping rather than manual field copying.
- Custom wart `NamedArguments`: when a call passes 2+ arguments of the same type, pass them by name or it will not compile.
- Tapir endpoint definitions live in `lib/api/shared/`, not `server/`.
- No external API calls in tests (testcontainers Postgres + fakes).
- Add/update tests for every change, following the existing specs for the files above (there are matcher, DAO, repo, action, controller, service, and web component specs already).
- The repo is PUBLIC: commit messages and the PR description must contain NO PII (no real bank names, account numbers, merchant names, amounts, or filenames) and NO claude.ai session links.

## Spec deviations

This spec was written from reading the current code. If while implementing you find a stated assumption about the existing code is wrong (a type, signature, column, or behavior differs from what is described here), do NOT force the spec to fit. Adapt to what the code actually requires, keep the intent, and clearly call out each such deviation and the reason under a "Spec deviations" heading in the PR description.
